title: Community Onboarding FAQ
claim: Members can select channels and roles through onboarding; the documented setup requires seven default channels, including five writable by everyone, and desktop administration.
limitations: Documentation establishes advertised behavior, not adoption benefit. Its displayed update date is older than access date; no hands-on Discord test was performed.

title: Blocking & Privacy Settings
claim: Discord documents server-level DM controls, blocking and friend-request permissions; shared-server members can send DMs by default.
limitations: Describes controls and documented defaults, not their effectiveness against harassment or every account-age-specific exception.

title: AutoMod FAQ
claim: AutoMod supports keyword/spam rules, blocking, alerts and timeouts. Built-in word lists and spam filtering are documented as English-only, while custom keywords support other languages.
limitations: No independent accuracy, false-positive or moderator-workload measurements; capability does not establish moderation sufficiency.

title: Forum Channels FAQ
claim: Forum channels organize posts with titles, tags, guidelines, search, list/gallery layouts and inactivity handling; documentation requires Community mode.
limitations: Older displayed update date. Do not infer that titled discussions automatically improve participation or that eligibility cannot change.

title: Server Onboarding Help - Unsolved
claim: A server administrator reports having to guide newcomers to Show all channels despite believing role and onboarding permissions were configured correctly.
limitations: Single self-selected support report; cause and current reproducibility are unverified. Relative dates were displayed, so no exact publication date is assigned.

title: Discourse Chat
claim: Current chat documentation describes thread titles/tracking, Quote to topic, channel moves, configurable retention and category-derived access.
limitations: The linked page also contains community replies; capability claims here use the maintained documentation post, not every reply.

title: Moving conversations from chat to topics
claim: Participants discuss losing authorship/notification continuity when quoting chats into topics; staff also describe curation and summarization as a useful deliberate transition.
limitations: Historical qualitative discussion with conflicting preferences; not proof that all reported limitations persist in 2026 or a representative usability study.

title: Phone Number Privacy and Usernames
claim: Signal separates phone visibility from discovery and permits contact initiation through exact usernames, QR codes or links, but still requires a phone number and offers no searchable username directory.
limitations: Capability documentation, not proof of anonymous operation or optimal discoverability. Existing contacts can already know a number.

title: How to create and share call links
claim: Reusable call links have optional administrative approval, deletion and expiry after 90 days unused; participants need Signal.
limitations: Not a browser guest-calling guarantee and not a benchmark for call reliability or participant capacity.

title: New Ways to Organize Events in WhatsApp Communities
claim: WhatsApp announced group event responses/reminders and grouped announcement replies with muted notifications.
limitations: Vendor launch announcement: useful feature evidence, but promotional adoption claims and the original rollout schedule are not independently verified.

title: New Updates to Polls and Sharing With Captions on WhatsApp
claim: WhatsApp announced single-vote polls, poll search, vote notifications and captions preserved or changed when forwarding media/documents.
limitations: Historical vendor announcement, not a complete account of current polls. Captions here mean accompanying message text, not live speech captions.

title: Telegram FAQ
claim: Telegram distinguishes groups from broadcast channels and cloud-synced chats from device-specific end-to-end encrypted Secret Chats; cloud group chats are not end-to-end encrypted.
limitations: The FAQ includes vendor security comparisons that this research does not adopt. No cryptographic audit or complete current feature census was performed.

title: Elements of Matrix
claim: Matrix federates room events across homeservers, with account identifiers containing a username and homeserver domain; bridges add another trust and identity surface.
limitations: Conceptual documentation, not evidence that moving a community transfers accounts or provides seamless portable identity.

title: How to Ensure You Have a Recovery Key
claim: Encrypted-history recovery uses a key distinct from the account password; losing both the key and verified devices can require an identity reset and lose access to old history.
limitations: Specific Element recovery workflow; does not prove all E2EE systems require identical UX or quantify recovery failure rates.

title: Opportunities and Challenges of Automatic Speech Recognition Systems for Low-Resource Language Speakers
publisher: Reitmaier et al., ACM CHI 2022; author-hosted paper
claim: Participatory research with isiXhosa and Marathi-speaking communities identifies the value of voice messaging, difficulty retrieving recordings and language/context challenges in transcription.
limitations: Situated qualitative fieldwork, not a representative global survey or evaluation of present-day WhatsApp or speech-recognition accuracy. Recommendations about live captions are extrapolations.

title: Our Most Requested Feature Yet
claim: Stoat announced video/screensharing, call/message sounds and push on several platforms; release notes acknowledge 720p30 sharing, Wayland audio issues and pending granular notification controls.
limitations: Vendor release claims were not hands-on verified. This later release supersedes historical assertions that the product simply lacks mobile voice or push.

title: [Mobile] Hangups and jank
claim: Several users report confusing mobile navigation, stale sent states, missing updates and notifications during attempts to move from Discord.
limitations: Small self-selected discussion preceding the July release. Evidence of harmful failure modes, not their persistence or prevalence today.

title: Encryption and new non-techie users
claim: A person inviting family recalls encryption/recovery friction; replies describe improvements and QR verification rather than unanimous rejection of encryption.
limitations: Recollection without a reproducible current bug and with differing responses. Relative dates were shown; does not justify recommending plaintext.
